To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the trace element contents in several rat tissues are different in spontaneously hypertensive and normotensive rats.
the inorganic contents of several tissues were different for the hypertensive rats compared with the healthy rats.
in the tissues studied there were differences between the inorganic contents of healthy and hyperten-sive rats for most of the elements studied.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the study of the inorganic content (major, minor and trace elements) in tissues of spontaneously hypertensive rats and the development of a multi-element method by inductively couple plasma-mass spectrometer for the analysis of the inorganic components in biological tissues.
the study of the inorganic content in healthy and hypertensive rats, and the results are discussed
the determination of inorganic content of rat tissues, especially those elements that are involved in the pathogenesis of hypertension.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the inorganic contents of tissues from spontaneously hypertensive and Sprague-Dawely rats are significantly different.

, with a few exceptions, the trace element contents of tissues from spontaneously hypertensive and normotensive rats are similar, and that there is no general increase in the inorganic content, or in the trace element content, of tissues from the spontaneously hypertensive rats.
the concentrations of all the elements determined are significantly different between the two groups of rats for at least one of the tissues examined.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the trace element concentrations in the kidney and liver of the hypertensive rat are different from those of the healthy rat.
the inorganic contents of most tissues are similar for both groups of rats, except for a few tissues and/or elements.
the trace elements in hypertensive rat tissues were not generally higher than those in healthy tissues.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the inorganic content can be used as a marker of the physiological condition of a tissue.
the concentrations of most elements are different in hypertensive tissues, and that these differences may be important in the pathogenesis of hypertension.
the concentrations of most elements in tissues from the hypertensive rats were higher than in the healthy ones.
